findings.gate: Craft Core — Authority and conflict handling (explicit on-page constraint from Ch06); Reader-trust invariant 3 (injuries and costs persist)

draft_evidence.quote: Karis's boxes were on three backs — Brom's, Lira's, his own — and the kit's case on Vastin's, who had not been asked and had picked it up at the fork-stone without a word. Lira ahead. Brom on the foot, which walked, as she had said it would.

comparison_evidence.quote: "Brom. That shoulder's been mended twice and I said not three times this season … It's bound, and it's held under the binding, and it's holding because you've carried it and not used it, and that's the whole of why it's holding. Inside walls you'll want to use it. Don't. Not a door, not a box, not a man."

findings.consequence: Introduced by the F-001 repair. Removing the mule required its load to go somewhere, and the draft puts a box on Brom's back on the morning after Oryn priced him — using the word she used. Her instruction is one chapter old, is the most quoted speech in Ch06, and names a box specifically; STATE_RUNNING After Ch06 records it as 'never use the shoulder inside', and the Ch14 log still carries 'the shoulder carried, bound fresh yesterday', so the not-used state is meant to persist for another eleven days. The same sentence makes the collision visible by citing her terms for the foot in the next breath ('Brom on the foot, which walked, as she had said it would') while silently breaking her terms for the shoulder. Lira is the secondary case: her arm is at day fifteen of the fifteen Oryn named, with 'don't spend it because you've got it' said to her directly, and she takes a box too. Meanwhile the three uninjured or unpriced members carry least — Karis has 'the flat under her arm', Seln is 'not anywhere he could point to', and the crew's most careful counter of costs does not price the redistribution at all, which is out of character for this narrator and reads to a returning reader as the healer's terms being forgotten the day she left.
findings.repair_target: Redistribute the load so it does not land on the priced shoulder and the fifteen-day arm — Cael and Seln take the boxes, Karis keeps the flat, Vastin keeps the case he picked up — or, if Brom must carry, have the narrator price it on the page: Brom taking it on the good side, or refusing it, or Cael counting what it costs against what a healer said at a fire. Whichever way, one clause should register that the terms exist, since the sentence already invokes them for the foot. Note that this reading also needs to be applied to Ch08, which still carries the mule five times.

strengths: Every one of the nine strengths recorded at r1 survives at its cited line, unaltered. The repair pass was genuinely targeted: it did not sand anything away, and it did not opportunistically rewrite prose outside the findings.

The F-005 repair improves the passage it corrects rather than merely fixing it. Line 21's restored staging — 'with her hands taken back, after he had told her the reading with his own hand on her wrist' — makes the order land as something Oryn said while withdrawing, which is a harder and better beat than the r1 version, and it puts the correct span ('three times in eighteen days, two of them running') inside the same sentence without ever sounding like a correction.

The mule repair at line 9 turns an accounting fix into characterisation. 'the kit's case on Vastin's, who had not been asked and had picked it up at the fork-stone without a word' converts a load-distribution problem into the chapter's first evidence that Vastin has decided something, and it sets up line 9's later observation that he has moved from the back of the column — two beats the r1 draft did not have.

The F-011 repair is a net gain in pressure. 'the light on its crown still there when the colour had gone' is stronger than the explanation it replaces, because the reader now supplies the inference the r1 draft stated, and it sits one line before 'He did not look at it' without contradicting it.

Line 23's restored contact form is not a bare revert. 'between him and the post' does the work of transposing Oryn's lying-down form to a seated road-side reading without asserting a new form, which is exactly what the r1 repair target asked for — and it is the reason R2-F-001 is a two-clause repair rather than a structural one.

The narrowed confession at line 89 loses nothing. Removing the falsified file and the ordered inquiry leaves 'I was not — at fifty-one, with a career behind me — going to be the man who decided that. I sent it up. I let it become a designation', which is a cleaner and more damning admission because it is entirely about what he chose rather than about paperwork, and 'Not the instrument. The man who declined to be one, and called it procedure' now has nothing standing in front of it.

The fixed log reproduces byte-for-byte, including the card's American 'color' against the narration's 'colour' at line 105, with the exception recorded rather than the line quietly altered. The author correctly declined to solve a packet-level problem inside the prose.

Reader standard remains clean and, more than clean, affirmatively good: zero banned words, no violence, no injury, no gore, no sexual content, and a chapter whose moral centre is a man naming his own evasion as an evasion, being neither excused nor asked for forgiveness, and a nineteen-year-old choosing to keep a promise and tell the truth about being afraid.
